title: Predictive Cost Alignment Assistant (PCAA) — product brief and launch playbook
author: Lina Morales
content:
Summary

This document describes the Predictive Cost Alignment Assistant (PCAA): a developer-facing product that recommends runtime fidelity, batching, and routing policies to meet customer cost targets while preserving response quality and latency SLOs. PCAA is intended to live as a first-class product offering in Redwood Optimize and as an embeddable advisor in the Redwood Console and SDKs.

Goals

- Reduce median per-token and per-request cost across customer workloads by 18–30% within 90 days of adoption.
- Provide deterministic recommendations that preserve 95% of baseline quality metrics (per-prompt evals) while meeting user-configured cost ceilings.
- Offer an audited decision trail for every recommendation to satisfy enterprise compliance and sales needs.

Problem statement

Customers building LLM features need predictable unit economics. Today they tune batching, KV caching, quantization, and model variant selection manually, which is error-prone and brittle across traffic patterns. Product teams request an assistant that: (a) predicts cost/latency tradeoffs for configuration changes, (b) suggests safe rollouts, and (c) ties recommendations to measurable impact in the Console and billing.

Product overview

PCAA combines offline workload analysis, a lightweight simulation engine, and an online signal adapter that watches real traffic. It produces per-route recommendations and an optional auto-apply mode (with safety gates). PCAA has three surfaces:

1) Console Advisor Card: interactive recommendations and simulated impact preview.
2) SDK/CLI Advisor API: programmatic query for recommended config sets.
3) Optimize Integration: batch jobs that surface global recommendations across tenants.

Key capabilities

- Predictive cost simulation: given a sample of historical requests (20k requests minimum), PCAA simulates cost and latency for permutations of batching, model variants, and quantization profiles.
- Fidelity-aware optimization: objective is configurable (cost-minimize subject to quality delta, or quality-maximize subject to cost delta).
- Safety rollouts: built-in canary recipe with automatic rollback triggers tied to telemetry signals (error rate increase > 0.5%, latency P95 drift > 30%).
- Audit trail: every recommendation stores the input prompt slice, the simulation parameters, and delta estimates.

Non-goals

- PCAA will not replace low-level runtime kernel selection or the serving runtime scheduler. It provides guidance and optional policy automation, not kernel-level optimization.
- PCAA will not provide content-level safety remediation; it will surface safety regressions but will not alter model outputs.

Requirements (high level)

Table: minimal acceptance criteria (rows)
| Requirement | Threshold | Owner | Notes |
|------------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Sample size for reliable simulation | >= 20,000 requests or 48 hours of traffic | product/eng-applied-ml | If sample smaller, fall back to conservative recommendations. |
| Simulation error bound (cost) | < ±6% vs measured | applied-ml | Validated during canary runs. |
| Quality regression guardrail | <= 5% drop on configured eval set | research | Automatically flag recommendations that violate this. |
| Canary rollback conditions | error rate +0.5% or latency P95 +30% | eng-sre | See rollout recipe. |

Design notes

Architecture overview (text diagram)
- Ingest: historical request collector (redwood-ingest-worker) fetches traces and anonymized prompt slices.
- Simulation: predictive-sim engine (rwd-pcaa-sim) runs vectorized throughput/latency/cost models.
- Policy store: recommendations persisted in config-store with versioned audit metadata.
- Execution: optional auto-apply service invokes Redwood Routing Controller to apply batching/variant policies.

Decision tradeoffs

- Model-level recommendations are conservative for enterprise tenants with private deployments: the system defaults to advisory-only for tenants flagged as restricted.
- Quantization suggestions are gated by measured eval deltas and explicit customer opt-in for quality-sensitive routes.

Telemetry and observability

Required telemetry signals:
- per-request token counts, model variant id, quantization profile id
- latency histogram (P50/P95/P99), error class counts, and cost attribution (tokens * cost-per-token profile)
- quality drift signals: shadow-eval pass/fail rates per prompt-set

Dashboard surfaces:
- Console: PCAA Recommendation Card showing predicted savings, confidence band, and most-risky prompts.
- Alerts: canary-failure alert if rollback conditions met.

API examples (pseudo-SDK)

Request recommendation (Python-like pseudo code):

r = client.pca.assess_route(
  route_id="tenant-123/order-summarize",
  sample_window_days=7,
  objective={"cost_ceiling_usd_per_1000": 0.60, "max_quality_loss_pct": 3},
  modes=["conservative","aggressive"]
)
print(r.recommendations)

Sample response (fields explained):
- recommendations: ordered list of config candidates with predicted_cost, predicted_latency_p95, quality_delta_pct, confidence_score, audit_id
- simulation_artifacts: link to stored artifact (for audits)

Safety rollout recipe (numbered steps)

1. Create recommendation in Console and mark as advisory.
2. Run dry-run simulation (Console button) to validate artifact against last 24h of traffic.
3. Schedule canary: 1% traffic for 2 hours under the recommended policy.
4. Monitor PCAA canary dashboard. If error rate increases >0.5% or latency P95 increases >30% -> automatic rollback.
5. If stable, expand to 10% for 24 hours, then to 50% for 48 hours, then full rollout.
6. Post-rollout validation: compare billing delta and eval delta after 7 days; create postmortem if cost savings < 60% of predicted or quality loss > allowed threshold.

Data privacy and compliance

- PCAA must not persist raw customer prompts for restricted tenants. For restricted/private deployments, the ingest pipeline performs on-host feature extraction and only stores anonymized artifacts.
- Audit entries include hashes and algorithmic summaries instead of PII.

Pricing & packaging guidance (internal commercial notes)

Offering tiers:
- Advisor (self-serve): Console recommendations, simulation preview, and manual apply. Included in Redwood Optimize Standard.
- Advisor Pro (paid add-on): Auto-apply runbooks, enterprise audit trail retention (12 months), and API rate limits for large-volume customers. Priced as percentage uplift on Optimize contract (suggestion: 7–12% ARR uplift).
- Integrator (professional services): Custom prompt-set calibrations, on-prem deployable simulation workers, and SLA-backed rollout assistance. Priced per engagement.

Suggested sales pitch bullets for AE enablement:
- Predict the cost impact of candidate changes before they reach production.
- Safely reduce unit economics without manual trial-and-error.
- Full audit trail supports compliance-sensitive customers.

Roadmap and milestones (quarterly)

Q4 2026 (pilot)
- Internal pilot with three strategic customers. Deliver Console advisor and simulation engine.
- Validate simulation error bound on customer workloads.

Q1 2027 (beta/public)
- Public beta, SDK surface, and basic auto-apply with safety gates.
- Integrate with Optimize batch recommendations.

Q2 2027 (GA)
- Billing hooks and audit-retention for Advisor Pro.
- UI polish and canary automation templates.

Q3 2027+ (expansion)
- Add per-prompt sensitivity mode, tighter integration with model onboarding to use model-specific fidelity profiles, and enterprise on-prem simulation option.

Launch checklist (checkbox-style bullets)

- [ ] Documented API contract and SDK stubs
- [ ] Console recommendation card implemented and user-tested
- [ ] Canary dashboard and alerting rules defined in monitoring repo
- [ ] Legal/finance pricing note approved and SKU created
- [ ] Pilot customers signed and success criteria agreed
- [ ] Security review completed (data flows and retention)

Appendix: acceptance test checklist

- End-to-end canary run against a test tenant with seeded traffic and synthetic prompts. Recorded metrics meet canary pass conditions for 48h.
- Simulation artifacts produce predicted cost within ±6% of measured cost for three separate traffic shapes (spiky, uniform, diurnal).
